title: Mortara wins Norisring Race 1 after Ekström’s lunge ends the Mercedes lead
dek: Edoardo Mortara won DTM Race 1 at the Norisring from sixth on the grid, 0.531 seconds ahead of Audi team-mate Green, after Ekström’s collision removed Wickens and spun pole-sitter Vietoris.

chapters.title: Mercedes’ living room, with the championship leader in residence
text: The DTM reached the Norisring on 25–26 June for the fourth of its nine race weekends, and Mercedes-AMG arrived as the favourite at a circuit it treats as home. Robert Wickens led the championship on 58 points, three clear of Marco Wittmann on 55, even though he had not yet won a race in 2016. Mercedes had not been beaten there in the official results since 2002.

Nothing about the form guide was simple. The 2.3-kilometre street circuit is the shortest on the calendar, a track of a few tight corners where a mistake meets a wall. Wickens called Mercedes’ redesigned C 63 DTM a lottery: the reworked upper bodywork had changed the airflow and downforce, helping on some circuits and hurting on others, as at the Red Bull Ring. Six races had produced six different winners: Mortara, di Resta, Wittmann, Glock, Molina and Auer; the order behind Wickens was tight, with Ekström on 46, Green on 45, Mortara on 44 and di Resta on 43. Wittmann, the 2014 champion, was racing on home ground.

chapters.title: Vietoris takes pole in a session decided by hundredths
text: Saturday’s 20-minute qualifying session was a frantic one, with two tenths of a second covering the top eight. Christian Vietoris put his Mücke Mercedes on pole with a 48.144 at about the halfway point, a lap nobody could beat. He had said the car was good but that he was not fully comfortable with the clutch for the start.

Ekström’s Abt Audi was 0.038 seconds slower and took the other front-row place, with Jamie Green’s Rosberg Audi 0.050 off in third. Wickens, fastest in second practice, was fourth at 0.106, and Bruno Spengler’s MTEK BMW was the first of the BMWs in fifth, 0.113 off the pace and the only one in the top ten. Edoardo Mortara, quickest in the first practice session, lined up sixth, with Paul di Resta, Lucas Auer, Mike Rockenfeller and Nico Müller completing the top ten.

BMW struggled against Mercedes and Audi on the street circuit. Timo Glock, Augusto Farfus, Wittmann and Maxime Martin were 11th to 14th, which left Wittmann, the championship’s second-placed driver, 13th on his home track. Adrien Tambay was 15th, Gary Paffett 16th and Maximilian Götz 17th. The back of the grid was formed by Molina, Scheider, Blomqvist, da Costa, Juncadella and Tomczyk, with rookie Esteban Ocon in 24th place, 0.430 seconds from the top.

chapters.title: Vietoris holds on, Wickens takes second and Tambay starts climbing
text: Vietoris got away cleanly. Ekström challenged him around the first corner, but the Mercedes was still ahead through the Schöller chicane and led the field on the opening lap, with Wickens soon relieving Ekström of second place. That looked like the start of an afternoon to Mercedes’ taste, while Green lost two places at the start and Mortara made up two from sixth to run fourth.

The midfield was busier than the front. Tambay worked his Rosberg Audi up from 15th with a string of overtaking moves, and the Audi pair of Rockenfeller and Müller were running eighth and ninth when Müller braked too late at the end of the start-finish straight and hit the back of Rockenfeller. Müller took the blame, and neither car recovered, with Rockenfeller finishing 19th and Müller 21st in the heat of about 30 degrees in the shade.

chapters.title: Ekström’s attack on Wickens spins the leader
text: The race turned on lap 20, roughly 16 minutes into the 40. Ekström went to the inside of Wickens under braking for the Grundig hairpin at the end of the start-finish straight, Wickens closed the door, and the two cars touched. Ekström then slid on into the leading Vietoris and spun him around. Wickens was stranded on the spot, Ekström’s race was over as well, and Vietoris resumed with a damaged car and dropped far down the order. The safety car was deployed, and Mortara, Green and di Resta led the field behind it.

The reaction was heated. Ekström said he was sorry for Vietoris, who had been an innocent victim, but blamed Wickens for closing the door and costing him braking. Wickens answered that Ekström was behaving “like a baby”, and Vietoris was in no mood to hear an apology. Audi’s DTM boss Dieter Gass called it a racing accident of the kind that happens often at the Norisring, and said it had not been Ekström’s fault alone, although he admitted the team would have preferred to celebrate its first Norisring win since 2002 differently.

chapters.title: Mortara resists Green as Audi ends 14 years of waiting
text: Mortara had only to keep Green at bay. The Rosberg Audi sat on his gearbox through the final laps without attacking: Green said he was quick enough to pass but did not want to put the Audi one-two at risk and needed the points. Mortara crossed the line 0.531 seconds ahead, and di Resta was only 0.372 behind Green in third, the best Mercedes after the collision had cost the brand its two leading cars.

Wittmann was fourth, 4.135 seconds behind the winner and the best of the BMWs on his home track, from 13th on the grid, and Spengler and Martin made it three BMWs in the first six. Tambay was seventh after starting 15th, Götz eighth, and da Costa climbed from 21st to ninth. Vietoris rescued tenth place and a single point, ahead of Farfus, Tomczyk, Auer and Glock. Besides the leaders in the crash, only Ocon failed to finish, parking his Mercedes in the pits.

For Audi it was the first Norisring victory since 2002, ending a Mercedes run at the street circuit that stretched back to 2003, and Mortara became the first driver with two wins in 2016. He moved to the top of the championship on 69 points, two clear of Wittmann on 67 and six ahead of Green on 63, while Wickens dropped from first to 58 points, level with di Resta.

facts.v: Mortara’s victory ended a Mercedes run at the street circuit that stretched back to 2003 and gave Audi its first win there in 14 years.
